topicTitle: Internal Energy and the First Law

questions.prompt: State the first law using \(Q>0\) into the system and \(W>0\) done by the system.
questions.answer:
With \(Q>0\) into the system and \(W>0\) done by the system, the first law is
\[
\Delta U=Q-W
\]

questions.prompt: A system receives \(300\,\mathrm{J}\) of heat and does no work. Find \(\Delta U\).
questions.answer:
No work is done, so
\[
W=0
\]
Using
\[
\Delta U=Q-W
\]
\[
\Delta U=300-0=300\,\mathrm{J}
\]

questions.prompt: A gas absorbs \(500\,\mathrm{J}\) of heat and does \(120\,\mathrm{J}\) of work. Find \(\Delta U\).
A gas releases \(200\,\mathrm{J}\) of heat and has \(150\,\mathrm{J}\) of work done on it. Find \(\Delta U\).
questions.answer:
The gas releases heat, so
\[
Q=-200\,\mathrm{J}
\]
Work is done on the gas, so work done by the gas is
\[
W=-150\,\mathrm{J}
\]
Then
\[
\Delta U=Q-W=-200-(-150)=-50\,\mathrm{J}
\]

questions.prompt: A system has \(\Delta U=250\,\mathrm{J}\) while doing \(90\,\mathrm{J}\) of work. Find \(Q\).
questions.answer:
Rearrange the first law:
\[
\Delta U=Q-W
\]
\[
Q=\Delta U+W
\]
\[
Q=250+90=340\,\mathrm{J}
\]

questions.prompt: An adiabatic expansion does \(400\,\mathrm{J}\) of work. Find \(\Delta U\).
A gas is compressed adiabatically by an external agent doing \(700\,\mathrm{J}\) of work on the gas. Find \(Q\), \(W\), and \(\Delta U\).
questions.answer:
Adiabatic means
\[
Q=0
\]
External work done on the gas is \(700\,\mathrm{J}\), so work done by the gas is
\[
W=-700\,\mathrm{J}
\]
Then
\[
\Delta U=Q-W=0-(-700)=700\,\mathrm{J}
\]

questions.prompt: A gas completes a cycle and does \(1.2\,\mathrm{kJ}\) of net work. Find net heat transfer and explain the sign.
questions.answer:
For a complete cycle,
\[
\Delta U=0
\]
so
\[
0=Q_{\mathrm{net}}-W_{\mathrm{net}}
\]
\[
Q_{\mathrm{net}}=W_{\mathrm{net}}=1.2\,\mathrm{kJ}
\]
The sign is positive because net heat enters the gas to supply the net work output over the cycle.

questions.prompt: A gas is taken from \(A\) to \(B\) with \(Q=Q_0\). Then it is returned to \(A\) adiabatically while work \(W_{\mathrm{on}}\) is done on it. Derive \(W\) for the first path in terms of \(Q_0\) and \(W_{\mathrm{on}}\).
questions.answer:
For the return path, the process is adiabatic:
\[
Q_{\mathrm{return}}=0
\]
Work \(W_{\mathrm{on}}\) done on the gas means
\[
W_{\mathrm{return}}=-W_{\mathrm{on}}
\]
Therefore
\[
\Delta U_{\mathrm{return}}=0-(-W_{\mathrm{on}})=W_{\mathrm{on}}
\]
Since the return path goes from \(B\) back to \(A\),
\[
\Delta U_{AB}=-W_{\mathrm{on}}
\]
For the first path,
\[
\Delta U_{AB}=Q_0-W
\]
so
\[
-W_{\mathrm{on}}=Q_0-W
\]
\[
W=Q_0+W_{\mathrm{on}}
\]

questions.prompt: A system undergoes three processes that return it to the initial state. Given \((Q_1,W_1)\), \((Q_2,W_2)\), and \(W_3\), derive \(Q_3\), and state which assumption makes the result possible.
questions.answer:
Because the system returns to its initial state,
\[
\Delta U_{\mathrm{total}}=0
\]
Using the first law for the three processes:
\[
(Q_1-W_1)+(Q_2-W_2)+(Q_3-W_3)=0
\]
Solve for \(Q_3\):
\[
Q_3=W_1+W_2+W_3-Q_1-Q_2
\]
The necessary assumption is that the three processes form a complete cycle, so the final state is the initial state and total \(\Delta U\) is zero.
